critique: 10, part one: stating intent precisely is as hard as writing the code. RCE-JEPA falsifier RJ-F2 (research.openie.dev/papers/rce-jepa/, Section 5): 'Writing sigma(iota) for the 7 reference applications costs more person-hours than writing their Forms by hand'.
what_rj_f2_registers_and_what_this_tests: RJ-F2 is stated in person-hours of authoring over the 7 reference applications. A timed authoring study needs participants, the 7 applications written as Forms, and a protocol for timing both halves; none of these is available in this run (apps/ holds 4 programs, all written by the RCE project, and no timing record exists). This run therefore does not test RJ-F2. It measures two proxies over the existing corpus: (A) the written size of the specification against the written size of the program it specifies, and (B) whether the written specification determines the program's behaviour, measured by mutants. Size is not effort; a corpus written by the RCE project is not a sample of outside authors.
engine: openIE-dev/rce a82a0348 (main), rce built from spec/checker of a commit whose spec/checker/src is identical to a82a0348 (scratchpad bin-main, release); the commit is written in every row
population: every .rce file of the scripts/corpus.py population rule (spec/examples, spec/examples-0.9/ok, programs, apps, book/listings not under refused/, stdlib/lib, and the conformance tests whose expectation is accept and which carry no fixtures) that rce check admits standalone and that carries at least one obligation; rows with the same shape hash (SHA-256 of rce fmt --nameless of the full file) are collapsed to the first in path order. Primary subset: files with an intent block or at least one example line. Files whose obligations are only check lines or contracts are reported as a second subset.

definitions.intent_text: the line beginning 'intent ' and every STRING line of its indented block (3.2 IntentLine = STRING NEWLINE): the words, not the tests
definitions.obligations: every example line, every check line (in an intent block or at top level), and every requires, ensures, decreases or ghost line (Appendix F contracts)
definitions.body: every remaining non-blank line that is not a full-line comment: the program the obligations constrain
definitions.measure: for each of intent_text, obligations, body: line count, and UTF-8 bytes with leading indentation and trailing comments removed (so indentation depth is not counted on either side); also the bytes of rce fmt --nameless of the bare program (body only), and the bytes and lines of rce emit python and rce emit rust of the bare program minus the shared runtime prelude (checked as a verbatim prefix, as in scripts/corpus.py)
definitions.bare_program: the file with the intent block, check lines and requires/ensures lines removed (decreases and ghost lines are kept, because removing a decreases clause can make a recursive program require change); a file whose bare program rce check does not admit is reported and dropped from the measurements that need it

part_A_metric: per file: ratio_bytes = obligation bytes / body bytes, ratio_lines = obligation lines / body lines, and the same with intent_text + obligations as numerator; reported as median, quartiles, min and max, overall and by class. Classes: origin (as scripts/corpus.py names it) and kind: machine (has a state region), command (fn main, no state region), library (neither).
part_A_reading: if the median ratio_bytes over the primary subset is above 1, the written obligations are larger than the programs they specify in this corpus; at or below 1, smaller. No other threshold.
part_B_subsample: every machine-kind file of the primary subset that has at least one example line (expected to be at least 20; if fewer than 20, the run reports that and stops part B) plus, as a secondary arm, every command-kind file with check lines
part_B_mutants: the five typed operators of scripts/corpus.py (rename, operator, literal, guard, type, imported from the rce checkout), seed 0x5eed_c0de_0010, up to 10 distinct mutants per operator per file, drawing up to 40 times per operator; a mutant is kept only if every changed or deleted line is a body line (the obligations are held fixed and only the program changes)
part_B_oracle: for each kept mutant M of file P: M_bare and P_bare as above. M_bare not admitted: 'not a program' (excluded). Machine kind: streams = the event lists of P's example lines, then 64 streams of 1 to 6 events drawn under the seed from a pool of event instances (every instance in P's example lines, plus for each declared event whose payload fields are all integer, bool or text: values from {0, 1, -1 when signed, the type's min and max, every integer literal of P and that literal plus and minus one} for integers, {true, false} for bool, {"", every string literal of P} for text, up to 64 instances per event); M_bare differs from P_bare if, on any stream, any step differs in outcome or state_hash (rce trace --json --streams), or if rce equiv --json reports not equivalent. Command kind: differs if rce run of the bare programs prints different bytes or exits differently. A mutant whose bare program differs is behaviour-changing; otherwise 'no difference found'.

part_B_metrics.catch_obligations: share of behaviour-changing mutants for which M (with all obligations) requires change while M_bare is admitted; pooled with a Wilson 95% interval, and per file
part_B_metrics.catch_examples_only: the same with M_ex = M with check lines removed (example lines only)
part_B_metrics.corpus_py_definition: for comparison with the figure on the RCE-JEPA page (317 of 392, 0.81): the same catch share when the denominator is restricted to mutants whose bare program differs on the example-line streams alone, which is what scripts/corpus.py's trace-head comparison sees
part_B_metrics.pinned_files: share of files in which every behaviour-changing mutant is caught by the obligations
part_B_metrics.uncaught_rows: every uncaught behaviour-changing mutant with its operator, the changed line, and the first distinguishing stream

part_B_reading: descriptive; no threshold. The gap between catch_obligations under the independent oracle and under the corpus_py definition measures how much the earlier figure depended on judging behaviour by the examples themselves.
known_biases: all programs were written by the RCE project, often with the examples written to exercise the code; obligation bytes count example expected values, which grow with state size; the stream oracle is bounded (64 streams of at most 6 events plus rce equiv's boundary alphabet) so 'no difference found' is not equivalence, and catch shares are over mutants the oracle can see; the five operators make single local changes, not the errors a person writing a wrong formula makes.
pilot: the harness may be run on programs/body/thermostat.rce alone while it is being written; that output is discarded and the full run is made once on the frozen harness, whose sha256 is written into RESULTS.md
reporting: results/files.jsonl (one row per file), results/mutants.jsonl (one row per kept mutant), results/summary.json, RESULTS.md; part two of the critique (Jevons-type economics) is a sourced note in RESULTS.md with no measurement
